newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU studies easing U.K. beef ban for some herds.
newsitem.headline: EU studies easing U.K. beef ban for some herds.

text.p: A group of European Union scientists has been asked to report by the end of May on a proposal to ease the British beef export ban for certified herds, European Commission spokesman Filippo di Robilant said on Tuesday.
Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler and Food Safety Commissioner Emma Bonino wrote a joint letter to the British government last week saying that a request to ease the ban was being considered, he said.
"We shall make sure that the examination is completed as promptly as possible," the letter, to British Farm Minister Douglas Hogg, said.

Britain proposed in February that the beef export ban should be partially lifted to allow exports of beef from Northern Irish and other herds guaranteed to be free of bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE).

European Commission spokesmen ruled out any early easing of the ban, saying that more veterinary inspections were needed to check whether Britain had complied fully with the Florence agreement, which provided a framework under which the beef ban might eventually be lifted.
Beef exports from Britain were banned by the EU in March last year after the brain-wasting mad cow disease was linked to the human equivalent Creutzfeld-Jakob disease (CJD)
A special sub-group of the European Union's standing veterinary committee was formed on Monday to consider lifting the ban on so-called certified herds, Robilant told Reuters.
The working sub-group of veterinary experts headed by the current chairman of the standing veterinary committee would meet for the first time on May 7.
"Their report will be considered by the full standing veterinary committee which is due to meet and give an opinion on June 11," Robilant said.
